intro: This week's five themes: IL-36R fills its first psoriasis pipeline slot, one Alzheimer's blood-test clearance ripples across four commercial wires, AAV gene therapy draws stricter FDA scrutiny over imaging findings, obesity differentiation shifts toward lean-mass preservation, and cell therapy manufacturing shows its first demand-side cooling signal.

narratives.headline: Vanda's imsidolimab gets EU orphan status, opening psoriasis's first IL-36R pipeline slot
narratives.detail: Imsidolimab (ANB019), Vanda's anti-IL-36R monoclonal antibody, received EU orphan designation for generalized pustular psoriasis (GPP). It becomes the first IL-36R-class pipeline asset tracked for psoriasis, alongside the already-approved spesolimab (Spevigo), also an anti-IL-36R agent. The designation fills a previously empty mechanism slot in the psoriasis landscape rather than displacing an incumbent.

narratives.headline: One Roche Elecsys pTau217 FDA clearance for Alzheimer's spawns four separate commercial-partner wires
narratives.detail: Roche's Elecsys pTau217 blood test received FDA clearance for Alzheimer's disease, and that single regulatory action has now generated four separate commercial wires: Labcorp and Quest each announced they'll distribute the test, and a fourth event names Eli Lilly in a co-branded pickup. It is one underlying clearance amplified by downstream partners, not four independent approvals. A third independent manufacturer clearance, beyond Roche and C2N, has not yet followed.

narratives.headline: Regenxbio's RGX-121 draws a second clinical hold over imaging-only findings, reading across AAV gene therapy
narratives.detail: Regenxbio's RGX-121 gene therapy was placed on a second clinical hold, triggered by an asymptomatic spine MRI abnormality with no reported clinical correlate — an imaging-only finding, not a symptomatic adverse event. The signal frames this as a stricter FDA posture on subclinical neuro-imaging findings that reads across the AAV gene-therapy class, not just this one asset. No other tracked AAV program is directly implicated yet. Watch whether a next AAV-class asset in a tracked indication draws a similar imaging-driven hold.

narratives.headline: Lumos Pharma's LUM-201 plus oral semaglutide enters Phase 2, competing on lean-mass preservation, not just weight loss
narratives.detail: Lumos Pharma's LUM-201, an oral GHSR agonist, is being combined with oral semaglutide in a Phase 2 trial (NCT07754045) explicitly positioned alongside bimagrumab- and apitegromab-style approaches — competing on preserved lean mass and physical function, measured via the SPPB endpoint, rather than total body weight loss percentage. This is a genuine, distinct differentiation axis in obesity, separate from the incretin-dominant mechanism landscape (GLP-1R/GIPR/GCGR). This lean-mass framing applies specifically to the LUM-201 program, not to other obesity deals reported this week.

narratives.headline: Cellares cuts ~100 staff after losing a major customer — first capacity-side cooling sign in cell therapy manufacturing
narratives.detail: Cellares cut roughly 100 staff after losing a large customer, marking the first capacity-side, as opposed to clinical or regulatory, cooling signal logged for autologous cell therapy manufacturing in the recent tracking period. It signals a shift from clinical and regulatory setbacks toward demand-side stress in cell therapy infrastructure. No specific indication or therapeutic asset is implicated; this is a manufacturing-capacity signal, not a trial result.
